# voxagent

> voxagent is a voice agent for the terminal. It records a spoken question with decibri, transcribes it on your machine with whisper.cpp, and prints the answer from a local model in Ollama. Your audio and your questions never leave your machine.

## Install

```
npm install -g voxagent
ollama pull llama3.2
voxagent
```

On its first run, voxagent also downloads the whisper model, about 150 MB.

## Requirements

- Windows x64, with the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable: https://aka.ms/vs/17/release/vc_redist.x64.exe
- macOS 14 or later on Apple Silicon
- Linux x64 with glibc 2.38 or later, such as Ubuntu 24.04 or Debian 13, with the Vulkan loader, the GNU OpenMP runtime and the ALSA library. On Debian and Ubuntu: sudo apt install libvulkan1 libgomp1 libasound2t64
- Node.js 18.3 or later, except Node.js 19
- Ollama, installed and running on the same machine: https://ollama.com
- A microphone, except with --file

Intel Macs, and ARM64 on Windows and Linux, are not supported.

## How it works

- Press Enter at the prompt and ask your question out loud.
- The recording stops 1.5 seconds after you stop speaking, at once when you press Enter again, after 8 seconds if no speech is heard, and at 60 seconds.
- A recording in which no speech is heard is not transcribed.
- voxagent transcribes speech as English, with the whisper model base.en.
- Press Ctrl+C to quit.
- The microphone is open only while a recording runs.
- Each question goes to the model on its own, without the earlier questions or answers.

## Options

- --model <name>: Ollama model to use (default: llama3.2)
- --device <id-or-name>: Input device to record from (default: the system default)
- --list-devices: List the available input devices and exit
- --file <path>: Answer one question recorded in an audio file, then exit
- --denoise: Reduce background noise before transcription
- --debug: Save each recording to debug-capture.wav in the current directory
- --help, -h: Show this help message
- --version, -v: Show version number

## Answering from a file

voxagent --file question.wav answers the question recorded in question.wav, then exits. The file can be WAV, AIFF, AIFF-C or FLAC. Without --file, voxagent needs an interactive terminal. With it, voxagent needs no microphone and no key presses. The exit code is 0 when the answer was printed, 1 when the file could not be read, held no speech, or could not be answered, and 2 when the command line was not valid.

## Privacy and the network

- Your audio is held in memory and passed to whisper.cpp in a process voxagent starts on your machine. No audio file is written, except with --debug.
- Your question is sent to the Ollama server at 127.0.0.1:11434, which answers it with the model you chose. With an Ollama cloud model, Ollama sends the question to its cloud service.
- The whisper model is downloaded once, about 150 MB, from the ggerganov/whisper.cpp repository on Hugging Face at a fixed revision, and checked against its SHA-256. It is stored in .voxagent/models in your home directory, and downloaded again only if that file is missing or has the wrong size.
- With --debug, each recording is saved to debug-capture.wav in the current directory, replacing the previous one. The file stays until you delete it.
- Apart from the model download, voxagent connects only to the Ollama server on your machine, and it needs no API key or account.

## Keeping the model loaded

Ollama keeps a model in memory for 5 minutes by default, and OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE, set when the Ollama server starts, changes that time, as the Ollama FAQ describes: https://docs.ollama.com/faq#how-do-i-keep-a-model-loaded-in-memory-or-make-it-unload-immediately
